chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Rehearsing "Don't Fence Me In" late at night
summary: Armstrong stayed late despite plans to go uptown, and the record became one of the biggest McRae worked on.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: thinking. Those guys were real deep thinkers. And Louie Armstrong never talked -- You know, one time he got mad. Just one time in his life, he got mad, when we did this -- I had to rehearse him at eleven o'clock in the night for him time to do a smash hit record (inaudible) "Don't Fence Me In with Velma (inaudible). (Inaudible). And he had to stay there late at night to rehearse the --
Go ahead. Just finish that line.
He didn't want to rehearse that late in the evening?

No, he didn't want to rehearse that late in the evening because he had a previous appointment. That was his night to run around. He wanted to get up to Harlem, you know, have a little fun. But he stayed and rehearsed it. It turned out to be one of the biggest things that I ever
